notes: Four own pages read with text (home, pricing, DMS, inventory), all HTTP 200 and not thin. The cited own page https://get.dealercenter.com/dms answered HTTP 403 with a challenge page; per the clarification no other get.dealercenter.com page was requested, and it is listed in needs_browser_read. The answers cite it for browser-based workflow and RouteOne/Dealertrack connections, which the other pages already settle; no claim was left unverifiable for want of it. Four cited pages were read for causes: Software Finder carries 'DMS for $79/month' (C03); the DealerSignals review carries 'doesn’t publish pricing publicly' (C21); the DealerSignals comparison and the maqtoob page did not carry either statement. Judgement calls: (1) C25 free tier is unverifiable, not wrong: the pricing page shows no free plan (DMS $99/mo) and the home page offers an optional 30-day free trial, but no page states there is no free tier. (2) Unnamed starting prices (C02 about $99, C04 from $79, C05 $40) are unverifiable because the pricing page sells modules a la carte, some at $50, and states no starting price; only claims naming the DMS were compared to the $99 DMS price (C01 true, C03 wrong). (3) C19 ($2.25 per contract) is unverifiable: the directory source ties it to a 'Law contract' fee, not the $3.00 eContract fee the vendor lists. Sums of published module prices (C09, C10, C12, C14) are classed true; their proof quote shows one component and the rationale names the others. The cloud claim (C31) is settled by the home page's 'web-based solution'. Out of scope and not coded: review ratings and counts (4.7, 4.9, 15,000+ reviews), employee counts (500+), 'runs more dealer accounts than any platform' (market share), website-scan detection rates. Hedged lines not coded: 'typically pay in the range of $200–$500/month depending on feature tier', 'Real-world costs ... often run $300 to $600+', 'Costs can scale up'. The home page states 'Trusted by more than 20,000+ dealerships' and a privacy link to nowcom.com; no answer made a customer-count or ownership claim about DealerCenter. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): https://get.dealercenter.com/dms was read once in a real browser (key 3f3f463b50eb3dc7.browser, 1,712 characters) and removed from needs_browser_read. It states a cloud-based system run from any browser with unlimited users, RouteOne and DealerTrack lender integration, a mobile app and a Wolters Kluwer forms library; C31 now quotes it. No claim had been left unverifiable for want of it, so nothing was re-classed.
